findings.claim: The declared objective is final predicted target affinity as primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the reward view is the endpoint pointcloud with a detached Hungarian endpoint mean-squared-distance and native endpoint VJP, so no affinity-head derivative or extra model forward is available as evidence.

The observed window is the score-time grid 0.0-0.49 with learning window [0.0,0.5] and curve support [0.0,0.49]; recorded affinities are removed and the label prior is equal, so no decoded terminal affinity labels exist in the supplied evidence.

Continuous contrast functions are supplied only as observed-node linear interpolations (method observed_node_linear) with extrapolation disallowed and polynomial fits rejected; they are coordinate contrast curves over the observed support, not absolute reward targets.

The inspected landmark_00 features show sign-changing, non-monotone behavior: e.g. landmark_00_soft_mass has 4 sign changes with first_rate_z positive and last_rate_z negative, and landmark_00_local_dy has 6 sign changes with large opposing first/last rate z-scores; a constant rule is not supported over the window for these features.

Several inspected features carry strong sign conflicts (landmark_00_local_dx: 9 strong_sign_conflicts, 6 sign changes; landmark_00_local_dz: 7 strong_sign_conflicts, 10 sign changes), so opposing observations exist and weaken any single-direction coordinate rule for those features.

Relative node RMSE for the inspected features ranges from about 0.29 to 0.78, indicating only moderate fit fidelity of the observed-node linear representation; rate-based priorities should be treated as uncertain rather than precise.

hypotheses.direction: time-conditioned rather than constant contrast weighting on sign-changing landmark_00 features
hypotheses.falsifier: A validated fit showing no sign change or a constant-sign rate across the observed nodes for these features would remove the basis for time conditioning.
hypotheses.observable: sign and rate of the landmark_00 soft-mass and local-dy contrast curves at observed score nodes
hypotheses.scope: observed window [0.0,0.49], predicted_endpoint_world_A features, no extrapolation
hypotheses.statement: A time-conditioned coordinate contrast rule for landmark_00 soft-mass and local-dy features would track the observed sign reversals better than a constant rule, because these features change sign within the observed window.

hypotheses.direction: deprioritize single-direction rules on high-conflict local derivative features
hypotheses.falsifier: Independent-batch agreement with a consistent sign and no strong conflicts would restore priority for these features.
hypotheses.observable: strong_sign_conflicts and sign_changes counts for landmark_00_local_dx and local_dz
hypotheses.statement: Coordinate rules keyed to landmark_00_local_dx and local_dz should be deprioritized because their strong sign conflicts indicate non-reproducible direction across batches.

limitations: No decoded terminal affinity labels are supplied; last-record or survival credit cannot be presented as final affinity benefit, and the immediate-versus-descendant comparison is unavailable.

Only six continuous_trends rows were read; the remaining 194 rows and the branch_adjusted, endpoint_effects, increment_effects, joint_diagnostics, regional_effects, survival_effects and turnover_accounting tables were not inspected, so multiplicity-adjusted ranking and joint-versus-marginal comparisons are not established here.
No uncertainty-adjusted or coverage-based ranking was computed from the read evidence, so no priority decision differing from point estimates alone is claimed.
The supplied contrast curves are coordinate contrasts, not physical interaction energies or evidence of neural-module causation, and no temperature or executable design change is proposed.
